messages:
Maya: Quick weekly CS check-in for NimbleHealth — token throughput trends look noisy: WoW +18%, QoQ +65%. Peak windows around 09:00 UTC show ~3x baseline QPS. Latency p95 climbed from ~120ms -> ~220ms during peaks. Error rate up to ~0.6% (mostly 502s/timeouts), baseline was ~0.12%. Spend pace is +35% WoW; projection shows they'll exceed their monthly commit if this continues. Noticed a lot of tiny prompts (1–3 tokens) causing high per-request overhead.

Ajit: Thanks, Maya. I filed a Dedicated capacity request (DED-451) but ETA is ~3w. In the short term we can tune batching and prefix caching. Can you share top routes / sample distribution for the last 24h?

Maya: Top routes (24h):
- /chat.user_message 48%
- /chat.quick_choice 23%
- /embed.search 15%
- misc 14%
Also ~62% of requests are <=3 tokens in the prompt.

Leo: If requests are that small, gateway-side micro-batching will help. Proposed staging config: ```batching_window_ms: 25
max_batch_size: 64
kv_cache_ttl: 300s```
Should smooth p95 and lower per-token cost. I'll run a controlled test on staging this afternoon.

Sam: Support saw customer-facing 502s between 09:02–09:18 UTC yesterday. Log excerpt: ```2026-03-19T09:05:12Z ERROR 502 upstream timeout req_id=abc123 route=/chat.user_message```
I already escalated to infra — they flagged a transient OOM on one GPU host. Collecting full traces now.

Maya: Action items:
1) Leo -> run batching test on staging today; tag me for quick validation.
2) Ajit -> confirm Dedicated timeline and offer temporary burst quota.
3) Sam -> gather 502 traces + timestamp-aligned metrics (GPU mem, OOMs, queue lengths).
4) Maya -> schedule enablement call with NimbleHealth to surface best-practices (suggest 2x 30-min slots).
If we can't bring error rate <0.2% by next Tue, propose a temporary rate cap to avoid billing surprises — everyone OK with that?

Ajit: Agree. We can also offer a one-week cost-smoothing credit if they sign up for a Dedicated trial. :+1:
